surfaces.part: teal border strip along the top row and right side
brown frame (rows 1-3) around a cream/white panel holding pink and green shapes

answer.evidence: The 16x16 cell is a flat, face-on panel. A teal row at the top (row 0) and a teal strip on the right edge border a brown frame (rows 1-3), a dark navy inner edge, and a cream/white field with pink and green motifs. The column scan at x=8 shows the brown frame at rows 2-3, then uniform cream (#f4ead0) from rows 4-14 with a single green pixel at row 11, and a brown bottom edge at row 15. There is no band ending in a front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse, no sloped roof or awning plane, and no visible contents inside an open container. Everything is drawn as a vertical face, so the cell reads as a front elevation with no top surface. It looks like a wall or window-panel tile rather than a gate, pavilion or building, so the structure kind fits poorly.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate on the right of the magenta bar is a tiny icon-like sprite, about one tile or less, with a white/teal panel and a small mark. It has no roof, walls or door, so it is not a whole building and does not match the building references. The facts show 16 distinct colours in total, against 185 and 66 for the references. The 16 visible tones per tile come from this one small icon, so they say little about building-level shading. The references have scalloped tile roofs with per-tile highlights, plaster speckle and shaded stonework, each at about 5-6 steps. The candidate has only about 3 readable shading steps and no material ramps or texture at building scale. Without a roof, wall and door it cannot be compared fairly, and it would look far thinner and more sticker-like beside the references.
